sections.h2: What is the address and schedule for the Saginaw County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Find it in the courthouse at 111 S. Michigan Avenue, Saginaw, MI 48602. The county's page shows weekday service from 8:00 until a quarter to five, with holidays off. Dial (989) 790-5270 to reach staff or send faxes to (989) 790-5278. The page still carries an old note about a lunch closing that ended in November 2022, so confirm the counter schedule by phone before a trip downtown.

The register is an elected keeper of every real property record in the county, keeps the index, and holds the original subdivision plats. Cities and townships call on it for liber and page references. Drafting and legal questions are off the table, and the quitclaim deed form page says so plainly.

Saginaw County spans 816 square miles, with the city of Saginaw as its seat. In 2020 it had 190,124 people and 85,953 housing units. Vacancy ran 8.7%, and 70.5% of the occupied homes belonged to their residents.

sections.h2: What will filing a document cost at the Saginaw office?
sections.html:
The recording charge is $30 a document under MCL 600.2567, however many pages it runs. An assignment or discharge that reaches several instruments picks up $3 per extra instrument. The fee page adds:

  • Page copies at $1, with a $5 certification per document.
  • Counter searches at $5 apiece.
  • A free public workstation inside the office.
  • Tax certification, which the County Treasurer handles.

Payment can be cash, check, money order, American Express, Discover, Mastercard or Visa, and cards add a fee. The checklist prices the Treasurer's certificate at $5 for the first five parcel descriptions, then $1 more per description. Before queueing at the register, stop at the Treasurer in Room 107 to learn if your instrument needs one.

sections.h2: Which formatting slips cause a Saginaw County rejection?
sections.html:
Saginaw County posts a long checklist built on Michigan's recording statutes. Each line carries a statute number, and a paper that fails any of them may come back unrecorded. These lines apply to deeds signed after April 1, 1997.

Saginaw County recording checklist, summarized from the register's quitclaim deed page
ItemWhat the checklist requires
Paper and typeWhite paper of at least 20 pounds, legible, in 10-point type or larger
Page sizeAt least 8.5 by 11 inches and no larger than 8.5 by 14
Margins2.5 inches clear at the top of page one and half an inch on every other side
Title lineFirst line names the single recordable event the paper evidences
SignaturesOriginal, in black or dark blue ink, with the name printed beneath
Notary blockDated acknowledgment, printed notary name and commission expiration
Legal descriptionPlat caption and lot number, or quarter section, section, town and range if unplatted

More lines follow. A street or post office address for the grantee is required, as is the drafter's name and address. Anyone signing after September 12, 2017 must black out the first five digits of a Social Security number, and foreign-language text needs a translation stapled behind it.

sections.h2: What does a Saginaw County deed say about transfer tax?
sections.html:
The checklist states a rate of $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. Either the deed itself shows total consideration or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit goes in with it. Where nothing is owed, the deed cites the exemption instead.

State law makes the seller responsible, with payment to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery (MCL 207.523). MCL 207.526 exempts a handful of transfers, for example a land contract that leaves title with the vendor, a boundary line adjustment with no payment, a mineral rights conveyance, and a spouse's conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entirety.

A few papers need extra proof. If a deed names a survivor, the death certificate must be certified and either recorded separately or cited by liber and page. A court order arrives certified and sealed by the clerk. A release or assignment points back to the original liber and page or document number.

sections.h2: Which Saginaw County places and roads shape local sales?
sections.html:
Saginaw County grew along the Saginaw River. A footpath that became the Saginaw Trail was authorized in 1819 and reached the city of Saginaw in 1841, one of Michigan's earliest roads. Today I-75 and I-675 pass through the area, with US 23, M-13, M-46 and M-47 linking the western suburbs to the airport at Freeland. Organized in 1835, the county includes the cities of Saginaw, Frankenmuth and Zilwaukee plus dozens of townships.

Saginaw Valley State University occupies part of Kochville Township, while Delta College serves residents from neighboring Bay County. Parcels can sit in one of about twenty school districts, from Saginaw Public Schools and Saginaw Township Community Schools to Frankenmuth, Chesaning Union and Birch Run Area Schools.

Saginaw County is part of a three-county metro area with Midland and Bay City. Residents had a median age of 41.3 in 2020. Michigan law leaves assessing and building permits with cities and townships, so a Saginaw County buyer or seller often deals with three offices: the township or city assessor, the county treasurer and this register.

sections.h2: What does the Saginaw County Treasurer add to a deed transfer?
sections.html:
Tax questions go to Room 107 in the same courthouse, open weekdays from eight to five. That office takes over delinquent real property tax, manages the Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund, and its head chairs the Land Bank Authority that handles tax foreclosed parcels. Without that certificate, state law keeps most warranty deeds off the record (MCL 211.135).

Back taxes can be paid at the counter, mailed to 111 S. Michigan Avenue or paid on the web around the clock. The web payment runs through an outside vendor that adds an access fee on the total. A card payment that is later reversed voids the payment, and the fees and interest reapply back to the original date. The Treasurer's page also describes a class action settlement, Fox v. Saginaw County, over surplus proceeds from tax foreclosure auctions between 2013 and 2020. Its claim deadline of July 16, 2026 has passed, so former owners who still have questions should contact the settlement administrator named on the county page.

sections.h2: How should a seller prepare for filing in Saginaw County?
sections.html:
Work through these steps in order:

  • Look up the current deed and legal description on the office workstation.
  • Learn from the Treasurer if a certificate applies, and pay for it apart from recording.
  • Show the price on the deed or prepare the valuation affidavit, and carry the tax payment.
  • Compare margins, ink, notary block and grantee address with the checklist.
  • Phone ahead about card fees and counter hours, and carry $30 per document.

After closing, the register passes transfers along to local assessors, and the buyer files a separate form with the assessor inside 45 days. Taxable value then resets to the state equalized value for the next year (MCL 211.27a).

faqs.q: What is the charge for recording at the Saginaw office?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document, plus $3 for every extra instrument one document assigns or discharges. Copies run $1 a page and certification costs $5.
No. Staff cannot prepare documents or offer legal advice. The quitclaim deed page sells access to a blank form for $5 plus an access fee, and sends owners to an attorney for legal help.

faqs.q: How is the Saginaw County transfer tax stated?
faqs.a: The checklist gives $8.60 per $1,000 of consideration. Sellers owe it, and an exempt transfer cites its exemption on the instrument.
The Saginaw County Treasurer issues it, and the register does not. The checklist fee is $5 for up to five descriptions and $1 per description past that.

faqs.q: What number do I call for the register?
faqs.a: Call (989) 790-5270. The office is in the courthouse, 111 S. Michigan Avenue, and faxes go to (989) 790-5278.
